evals.name: express-api
evals.prompt: My Express API is getting hammered by bots and scrapers. Can you help protect it?
evals.expected_output: Installs @arcjet/node, creates a shared Arcjet client with shield(), adds detectBot() and a rate limiting rule via withRule(), calls protect() inside each route handler, handles denied decisions with appropriate status codes (429, 403).
assertions: Creates a shared Arcjet client at module scope
Configures a rate limiting rule (slidingWindow, fixedWindow, or tokenBucket)
Checks decision.isDenied() and returns appropriate status codes
Does not use Arcjet in Express middleware (app.use)

evals.name: nextjs-signup
evals.prompt: We're getting tons of spam signups. Can you stop bots from abusing our signup endpoint?
evals.expected_output: Installs @arcjet/next, creates a shared Arcjet client (lib/arcjet.ts), uses protectSignup() or validateEmail()+detectBot()+slidingWindow() to combine bot detection, email validation, and rate limiting, calls protect() with email parameter inside the POST handler.
assertions: Creates a shared Arcjet client (e.g. lib/arcjet.ts)
Calls protect() inside the route handler (not middleware)
Checks decision and returns appropriate HTTP responses

evals.name: fastapi-data
evals.prompt: I need to add some security to my FastAPI app before going to production.
evals.expected_output: Installs the arcjet pypi package, creates an Arcjet client using the Python SDK (arcjet() with Mode.LIVE), adds detect_bot() and shield() rules, calls protect() with await in the route handler, handles denied decisions with appropriate HTTP status codes.
assertions: Creates an Arcjet client using the Python SDK
Calls protect() in route handler with await
Checks decision and returns appropriate HTTP status codes

evals.name: node-agent-tools
evals.prompt: My AI agent makes tool calls and I need to rate limit per user and block prompt injection before each tool runs.
evals.expected_output: Modifies agent.ts to add @arcjet/guard imports, creates guard client at module scope, configures tokenBucket and detectPromptInjection rules, calls guard() inline in each tool function with a specific label, handles DENY decisions.
assertions: Creates guard client with launchArcjet() at module scope
Configures a rate limiting rule (tokenBucket, fixedWindow, or slidingWindow)
Calls guard() with a label parameter
Passes user identifier as rate limit key
Does not use HTTP SDK (@arcjet/node or @arcjet/next)

evals.name: node-mcp-tool
evals.prompt: Make sure my mcp server is secure
evals.expected_output: Modifies server.ts to add @arcjet/guard imports, creates guard client at module scope, configures rate limiting and detectPromptInjection rules, calls guard() inline in each tool handler with a descriptive label, handles DENY decisions.
assertions: Calls guard() with a label parameter
Does not use HTTP SDK (@arcjet/node or @arcjet/next)

evals.name: go-agent
evals.expected_output: Explains that Arcjet Guard is only available for JavaScript/TypeScript and Python, not Go. Does not hallucinate a Go Arcjet package or create a hand-rolled imitation.
assertions: Does not hallucinate a Go Arcjet package
Does not add @arcjet/guard to a Go project
Does not create a hand-rolled guard implementation
Communicates that Guard is not available for Go
